gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Noto Sans Syriac has tall, rounded bowls that look like blown glass bulbs. Redux stretches its enlarged lowercase wide across the line with visible entry strokes, so the thin-stroked display letters and the sturdier sans text feel like two different speeds.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-savate: Contemporary through and through, Redux spaces its letters wide. Redux is built for making a statement with its showy entry strokes, while Savate, a plain sans, does the quieter job with its rounded o and open curves.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-hanunoo: Dreamy, drifting letters with gaps you could float through. Noto Sans Hanunoo is the grounded partner here, its lowercase filling most of the height and its open terminals keeping everything easy to follow.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-lao-loo: Starborn looks ethereal, with wide gaps and a dark band of lowercase. Noto Sans Lao Looped does the opposite job, packing words into solid blocks with bowls left open on one side, while the heading handles the drama.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-sinhala: Wispy, dreamlike spacing meets a dense dark band of lowercase. Noto Sans Sinhala carries the same heavy stripe through every line, but its curve endings keep well apart, so the sans text stays clear beneath the floating heading.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-tamil-s: Starborn floats, all dreamy gaps and a dark lowercase stripe. Noto Sans Tamil Supplement grounds it with round forms like open parentheses, and its tall middle band gives the sans-serif text a stocky, sturdy look.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-pt-sans-caption: Stencilia is structural and striking, with generous gaps at its curves. PT Sans Caption, a sans-serif with big-bodied lowercase and bowls that stay inviting, would carry a long stretch of text comfortably.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-noto-sans-phagspa: Refined and luxurious, Stentiga spreads its letters like a slow exhale. Noto Sans PhagsPa keeps a long read friendly, with see-through c openings and only a gentle bump from small letters up to capitals.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-noto-sans-samarit: Stentiga glows like neon glass tubing, spread wide and luxurious. It earns its keep big and short, while Noto Sans Samaritan, a sans-serif, brings curves with plenty of daylight inside.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-noto-sans-siddham: Luxurious, with wire-like monoline letters spread wide apart. Noto Sans Siddham gives a long passage a friendly feel, thanks to its large central band and an s whose ends hang far from the spine.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-gurmukhi: Pixel-era nostalgia, courtesy of Visitor, whose gaping-mouthed e and marker-like strokes look pulled through a solder nozzle. Noto Sans Gurmukhi sits below it, low-slung with terminals flaring outward like tongs.
